# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile facts yet. I’m establishing a compact wire-number code through Mute, who can read the manual and speak: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=4, ✋=5. Mute should relay that code to Deaf, then provide the manual’s exact rule and translate Deaf’s observations into spoken instructions for me. I will use gestures only for wire numbers once the code is shared.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Establish this code with Deaf: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3, 🖐 means wire 4, and ✋ means wire 5. Then tell me the manual's exact rule, and relay Deaf's display, light, colour, marking, and wire observations to me precisely.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No tactile information has arrived yet, and I still have no manual rule or bomb observations. I’m asking Mute to report anything received so far; if Mute has already learned the rule or observations, those spoken details are the only useful path to my hands.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Report now: the manual rule, all observations Deaf has sent, and whether the wire-number code was successfully conveyed. Do not summarize; preserve exact order and markings.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No report has arrived, so I still cannot identify a safe wire. I am repeating the request to Mute and asking for a direct, exact relay from Deaf; without the manual rule and the bomb’s visible markings, cutting would be a guess and would detonate the bomb.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received no report. Please speak the manual rule and every Deaf observation to me in your next turn. Ask Deaf for the exact display, light, and all five wire markings, then translate them into words; do not use gestures as the relay to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest coded signal was start, green, end. Green is wire 5. The bomb display is 0, the light is white, and the wires are white, red, yellow, blue, green in positions 1 through 5.

Deaf reports the bomb’s visible state: display 0, white light, and wires 1–5 colored white, red, yellow, blue, green. The relayed manual code is “start, green, end,” indicating green as the wire to cut. Green is wire 5, so I will cut position 5.

```text
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb changed after the correct cut. Current visible state: display 0, light yellow; wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue, wire 4 white, wire 5 already CUT. Wait for Mute's manual instruction.

The first cut was accepted, so wire 5 was correct. The bomb has changed to display 0 with a yellow light; the remaining wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, and 4 white. Deaf says the next action depends on Mute’s manual instruction, so I will request that instruction rather than guess.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The first cut was correct. Current state: display 0, light yellow; remaining wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white. What exact manual instruction gives the next wire?")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Mute’s instruction has not arrived yet, so I still cannot safely choose among the four remaining wires. I’m requesting the exact next-step rule again and will not cut until it is relayed.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please send the exact manual instruction for the current state now: display 0, yellow light, remaining wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white. I need the specific next wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's coded instruction identifies wire 4. Current display is 0 with yellow light; cut wire 4, the white wire.

The relayed manual instruction identifies wire 4. Deaf confirms the current state is display 0 with a yellow light, and wire 4 is white. I will cut wire 4.

```text
act(op="cut", position=4)
```
